text: Create an authored discovery lesson about the value of a digit in a two-digit number. Begin by counting ten individual cubes aloud, then visibly bundle those same cubes into one ten. Build twenty three from two groups of ten and three leftover cubes. Keep twenty three as the worked example while connecting the digit two to two tens worth twenty and the digit three to three ones worth three. Explicitly distinguish a digit counting groups from the quantity those groups represent. Ask for the value of four in forty two, wait six seconds, then count the four rods as ten, twenty, thirty, forty and explain the answer. Finish with the model of twenty three. Large concrete objects, progressive counts, slow sequential bundling and a visible connection from selected blocks to digit and value. No multiplication-by-ten lesson, trading, zero or hundreds. Warm Indian-English delivery using the existing local Piper voice; friendly and unhurried. This is an authored quality sample, not model-generated output or a complete Grade 5 curriculum lesson.
